games.title: Words to 100
games.skillName: Numbers to 100 in words and comparing with <, > and =
games.statutoryRequirement: Pupils should be taught to read and write numbers to at least 100 in numerals and in words; compare and order numbers from 0 up to 100; use <, > and = signs
games.instruction: Read it, then tap the right answer.
games.hint: Not quite. Look at the tens digit first, then the ones, and try again.

questions.ask: What is 'forty-seven' in numerals?
Which words show 63?
Which word is 90?
What is 'eighty-five' in numerals?
Which sign makes 56 ? 65 true?
Which sign makes 72 ? 27 true?
Which sign makes 40 ? 40 true?
Which is the greatest: 39, 93, 59 or 83?
Which is the smallest: 41, 14, 40 or 44?
Which of these is true?

games.title: Triple Dice Total
games.statutoryRequirement: Pupils should be taught to add and subtract numbers using concrete objects, pictorial representations, and mentally, including: adding three one-digit numbers
games.instruction: Add all three numbers, then tap the total.
games.hint: Not quite. Look for two numbers that make 10 first, then add the last one.

questions.ask: What is 3 + 4 + 5?
What is 6 + 2 + 8?
What is 9 + 1 + 7?
What is 5 + 5 + 5?
What is 8 + 7 + 2?
What is 4 + 6 + 9?
What is 7 + 3 + 3?
What is 9 + 9 + 2?
What is 2 + 8 + 6?
Which is the quickest way to add 7 + 5 + 3?

games.title: Fair Share Fractions
games.skillName: Finding fractions of a set or quantity
games.statutoryRequirement: Pupils should be taught to recognise, find, name and write fractions 1/3, 1/4, 2/4 and 3/4 of a length, shape, set of objects or quantity
games.instruction: Share them out fairly, then tap the answer.
games.hint: Not quite. Split the amount into equal groups, then count the groups you need.

questions.ask: What is 1/2 of 6?
What is 1/3 of 9?
What is 3/4 of 8?
There are 12 sweets. 1/4 of them are red. How many are red?
What is 1/2 of 14?
What is 2/4 of 8?
There are 12 eggs. 1/3 are brown. How many are brown?
What is 3/4 of 12?
What is 1/4 of 20?
Share 15 apples into 3 equal groups. What is 1/3 of 15?

games.title: Read the Scales
games.skillName: Reading scales for mass, temperature and capacity
games.statutoryRequirement: Pupils should be taught to choose and use appropriate standard units to estimate and measure length/height in any direction (m/cm); mass (kg/g); temperature (°C); capacity (litres/ml) to the nearest appropriate unit, using rulers, scales, thermometers and measuring vessels; compare and order lengths, mass, volume/capacity and record the results using >, < and =
games.instruction: Read it, then tap the right answer.
games.hint: Not quite. Check the units and count the steps on the scale, then try again.

questions.ask: Which unit would you use to weigh a bag of potatoes?
Which unit tells you how hot or cold it is?
Which unit would you use for a spoonful of medicine?
A thermometer goes up in 2s. It reads 1 mark after 20°C. What is the temperature?
A scale counts in 100 g. The arrow is 3 marks after 0. What is the mass?
A jug counts in 50 ml. The water is 2 marks above 100 ml. How much water?
Which sign makes 3 kg ? 5 kg true?
Which sign makes 40°C ? 14°C true?
Which sign makes 60 ml ? 60 ml true?
Which temperature is the warmest?

games.title: Pocket Money Shop
games.skillName: Using £ and p, combining coins and giving change
games.statutoryRequirement: Pupils should be taught to recognise and use symbols for pounds (£) and pence (p); combine amounts to make a particular value; find different combinations of coins that equal the same amounts of money; solve simple problems in a practical context involving addition and subtraction of money of the same unit, including giving change
games.instruction: Read it, then tap the right amount.
games.hint: Not quite. Add the coins one at a time, or count on to find the change.

questions.ask: How much is 20p + 20p + 5p?
Which two coins make 30p?
Which coins make exactly 50p?
You buy a 7p sweet with a 10p coin. How much change do you get?
You pay 50p for a 35p apple. How much change do you get?
You pay £1 for a 60p comic. How much change do you get?
How much is £5 + £2?
How many 10p coins make £1?
How much is 50p + 20p + 2p + 1p?
A pen costs 25p. How much do 2 pens cost?

games.title: Hours and Minutes
games.skillName: Minutes in an hour, hours in a day and comparing time
games.statutoryRequirement: Pupils should be taught to know the number of minutes in an hour and the number of hours in a day; compare and sequence intervals of time
games.instruction: Read it, then tap the right answer.
games.hint: Not quite. Remember there are 60 minutes in an hour and 24 hours in a day.

questions.ask: How many minutes are in an hour?
How many hours are in a day?
How many minutes are in half an hour?
How many minutes are in a quarter of an hour?
How many minutes are in 2 hours?
How many hours are in 2 days?
Which is the longest time?
Which is the shortest time?
Film A lasts 90 minutes. Film B lasts 1 hour. Which is longer?
Which of these would take the longest?

games.title: Corners and Faces
games.skillName: Sides, vertices, symmetry and faces of shapes
games.statutoryRequirement: Pupils should be taught to identify and describe the properties of 2-D shapes, including the number of sides and line symmetry in a vertical line; identify 2-D shapes on the surface of 3-D shapes [for example, a circle on a cylinder and a triangle on a pyramid]
games.instruction: Read it, then tap the right answer.
games.hint: Not quite. Count the sides or corners one at a time, then try again.

questions.ask: How many sides does a pentagon have?
How many vertices does a hexagon have?
How many vertices does a triangle have?
How many sides does an octagon have?
Which shape has 4 sides and 4 vertices?
What 2-D shape is on each end of a cylinder?
What 2-D shape is every face of a cube?
What 2-D shape are the sloping faces of a square-based pyramid?
Which capital letter has a vertical line of symmetry?
Which capital letter does NOT have a vertical line of symmetry?

games.title: Pattern Parade
games.skillName: Patterns and sequences of objects and shapes
games.statutoryRequirement: Pupils should be taught to order and arrange combinations of mathematical objects in patterns and sequences
games.instruction: Find the repeating part, then tap what comes next.
games.hint: Not quite. Find where the pattern starts again, then try again.

questions.ask: circle, square, circle, square, ... What comes next?
red, red, blue, red, red, blue, red, ... What comes next?
triangle, square, pentagon, ... What comes next?
star, moon, sun, star, moon, ... What comes next?
big, small, small, big, small, small, big, ... What comes next?
A, B, B, A, B, B, A, ... What comes next?
1 dot, 2 dots, 3 dots, ... What comes next?
up, down, down, up, down, down, ... What comes next?
cat, dog, fish, cat, dog, fish, cat, ... What comes next?
square, square, circle, circle, square, square, circle, ... What comes next?
